batch_intro:
Use `df` to answer the questions below. Build a dict named `answer` with keys {keys}.

{lines}
mode_categorical: What is the mode of `{column}` (most frequent category)?
stat_of_column: What is the {label} of `{column}`? Round to 2 decimal places.
which_larger_std: Which variable has the larger sample standard deviation: `{left}` or `{right}`? Assign the column name as a string.
which_larger_var: Which variable has the larger sample variance: `{left}` or `{right}`? Assign the column name as a string.
groupby_header: Use `df.groupby('{group_col}')` to compare the continuous variable `{value_col}` across levels of `{group_col}`.
groupby_highest_mean: Using `df.groupby('{group_col}')['{value_col}'].mean()`, which `{group_col}` has the highest mean `{value_col}`? Assign the group label as a string.
groupby_skew_gap: Which `{group_col}` shows the largest absolute gap between mean and median `{value_col}` (a possible skew signal)?
groupby_mean_value: What is the mean `{value_col}` for `{group_col}` = '{group}'? Round to 2 decimal places.
groupby_highest_std: Which `{group_col}` has the largest sample standard deviation of `{value_col}`?
groupby_median_value: What is the median `{value_col}` for `{group_col}` = '{group}'? Round to 2 decimal places.
hard_bimodal_plot_line: 1. Plot a histogram of `{column}` showing its bimodal shape, then set `plotted = True`.
hard_bimodal_plot: Plot a histogram of `{column}` (it should look bimodal). Then set `plotted = True`.
hard_bimodal_mode: What is the mode of `{column}` after rounding each value to the nearest integer (`df['{column}'].round().mode()`)? Assign the integer mode.
hard_bimodal_peaks: Estimate the two peak centers of `{column}` (the two modes of the mixture). Assign a sorted list of two integers (nearest whole numbers).
hard_bimodal_median: What is the median of `{column}`? Round to 2 decimal places.
hard_corr_plot: Create a correlation heatmap of the numeric columns in `df` (e.g. `plt.imshow(df.corr(), ...)` or similar), then set `plotted = True`.
hard_corr_pair: Which two numeric columns have the strongest absolute Pearson correlation (ignore the diagonal)? Assign a sorted list of their two names.
hard_corr_value: What is the Pearson correlation between `{left}` and `{right}`? Round to 2 decimal places.
hard_corr_positive: Is the correlation between `{left}` and `{right}` positive? Assign True or False.
hard_corr_plot_line: 1. Plot a correlation heatmap of the numeric columns, then set `plotted = True`.
